Represent Identity & Access in cross-functional architecture reviews and roadmap decisions. Lead and grow a small, high-caliber team — run regular 1:1s, set quality standards, give direct feedback, and develop engineers on security-critical systems. Protect operations where failures carry tangible stakes—from halted production lines to scrapped material and compliance risks. What you ship here has a direct impact on customers. Create and own difficult tradeoffs on IAM and access policy where tenant isolation and enterprise compliance are non-negotiable. Ship work that reaches customers quickly and reliably, with operational excellence as the default. jobs.title: Events Associate
jobs.description: Who we are Foundation models transformed text and images. Structured data - the largest and most consequential data format in the world - stayed untouched, until now. What LLMs did for language, we're doing for tables. We pioneered tabular foundation models: TabPFN v2 was a Nature cover story, has passed 3.5M+ downloads and 7,500+ GitHub stars, and runs in production from detecting lung disease with Oxford Cancer Analytics to preventing train failures with Hitachi . The hardest problems - millions of rows, real-time inference, entirely new modalities - are still open, and no one else is working on them at this level. We're a small, highly selective team of 40+ with backgrounds from Google, DeepMind, Meta, Apple, Amazon, Jane Street, and CERN, led by Frank Hutter , Noah Hollmann , and Sauraj Gambhir , and advised by Bernhard Schölkopf and Turing Award winner Yann LeCun. In July 2026, less than 18 months after our €9M pre-seed, we joined SAP as an independent frontier AI lab - same team, mission, and open-weights models, now backed by more than €1 billion over four years. ABOUT THE ROLE Want to work at the frontier of AI and shape the most forward-looking event formats globally? Events are where TabPFN meets the world, and one of our strongest channels. We show up at the most talked-about conferences across research and industry, in cities like New York, Seoul, Paris and Sydney, with one ambition: to be the name everyone remembers on the way home. And we create our own moments, from meetups and hackathons to executive dinners people want to be in the room for, where we lead the conversation on AI for tabular data. You will be at the heart of how our events come together globally. You work hands-on with our Founders office, who owns the events strategy, and alongside sales, research and DevRel. You make sure every detail is taken care of, so every event is flawless on the day and turns into real conversations afterwards. You'll learn how a fast-growing AI company runs its events, and grow with the program as it scales. Everything we do is AI-first. We use the latest tools and aim to run events smarter than anyone else, so you'll spend less time on spreadsheets and email chains and more time on the details that make an event worth attending. If you've ever wanted to take event management to the next level, this is the place. CORE AREAS OF IMPACT The events we run Industry & academic conferences: from large-scale trade shows to NeurIPS and ICML, wherever they take place around the world Side events & community meetups: the side event everyone talks about, and the meetups and hackathons where people build with TabPFN Executive dinners & briefings: small rooms, senior guests, real conversations, from Berlin to San Francisco What you'll do across all of them Help deliver events that bring our brand and product to life: Help shape our events strategy, sponsorships and creative concepts Help shape agendas, find speakers and spot opportunities to maximise our presence, with smart ways to get people curious and excited about TabPFN Run the logistics: venues, vendors, travel, booths and merch Set up invites, Luma pages and guest communication Support the team on site and make every guest experience seamless Help build playbooks and automations, and track what each event delivered Bring the vibe: dream up experiences people talk about, from activations and live demos to gamification, installations or the right DJ. If it makes the night, it's on the table Capture content on site that brings every event to life on our social channels WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR You're organised, calm under pressure and obsessed with the details guests notice. You bring a strong executor mindset and know how to build experiences for high-profile guests, from executives and researchers to media and senior partners, with the judgment to make every event feel seamless, elevated and deeply considered. You have: Essential Background 1-3 years of experience running events, ideally B2B, tech or conferences Hands-on experience with event logistics: venues, vendors, travel, guests Experience with executive dinners, conference booths or side events Great intuition and taste for what looks and feels good, you create experiences people remember and make everyone who didn't show up feel they missed out! A bias for action and experimentation: you'd rather test and learn than wait for a perfect playbook A strong collaborator: you coordinate smoothly with sales, research and DevRel An AI-first way of working: you use the latest tools to run events leaner and faster Structured and reliable: when you own something, it's handled Exceptional written and verbal communication skills Happy to travel 40%+ internationally What Makes You Special Experience in an early-stage startup or a fast-growing tech company You've worked with sales and know what makes an event useful for pipeline Familiarity with AI, ML or developer communities Experience with academic or research conferences A network of venues, agencies and vendors in Berlin, London or New York is a plus LOCATION Berlin, on-site, with frequent travel Life at Prior Labs You'll work alongside researchers and builders who hold themselves to a very high bar - in the quality of their work and in how they work with each other. We move fast and still take the time to do things right. Our teams are based in Berlin, Freiburg, and New York - when you're working on something as hard as TabPFN, being in the same room matters. But great people come from everywhere, and in exceptional cases we're open to remote, which usually means frequent travel to one of our offices. Wherever you're based, the whole company comes together regularly for offsites to build and celebrate together. Our Commitments The best products and teams are built by people with a wide range of perspectives and backgrounds. jobs.title: Senior Site Reliability Engineer - Ceph / On-Prem Cloud Storage (m/f/d)
jobs.description: Your Role You will help us build, operate and industrialize the storage foundation of our on-premise cloud platform. As part of a small, experienced team, you will own the Ceph clusters behind our block, object and file storage services – essentially the storage every customer workload eventually lands on. The platform is still actively being built, which means you will have real influence on the storage architecture, hardware lifecycle, automation strategy and technical direction. The role goes beyond Ceph itself: you will regularly work across bare metal, networking, OpenStack, Kubernetes and GitOps. As a Senior Engineer, you take ownership of your area and help make storage predictable, durable and highly automated as we scale into the petabytes Unser Tech Stack 🚀 · Ceph · OpenStack · Kubernetes · KVM · Linux · Bare Metal · Ansible · Terraform · Go · Cinder ·Neutron · Nova · RBD · Cilium · RGW/ S3 · Prometheus/ Grafana · FluxCD / ArgoCD · Git· Python · Claude Code · Cursor · Agentic Coding Tooling Your Responsibilities Design, operate and evolve our Ceph clusters for block, object / S3 and file storage - from CRUSH topology and failure domains to pool design, placement groups, erasure coding, capacity headroom and performance. Own the storage hardware lifecycle end to end – from qualification and burn-in through firmware, controller and disk health to OSD add/drain/replace, node retirement and hardware refresh. A key part of the job is automating these processes without creating tenant-visible impact. Automate the provisioning of storage nodes on OpenStack-managed bare metal , working with Ironic, RAID and disk configuration, SEDs, provider networks and VLANs. You will also own the artefact path around images, package mirrors, certificates and other dependencies needed to bring up clusters in environments with tightly controlled external connectivity. Run upgrades, rebalancing and reconfigurations as routine production operations, evolve our Infrastructure as Code and GitOps setup with Ansible, Terraform and FluxCD / ArgoCD, and make sure storage integrates cleanly with both OpenStack and Kubernetes. Own capacity planning and growth forecasting , use telemetry to understand real consumption, and build out monitoring, testing and failure-injection around performance, durability and security. AI-assisted engineering is simply part of how we work today. You use LLMs and agentic tools where they genuinely help – across development, testing, reviews, incident triage, knowledge retrieval or automation - and help us push further into self-healing and auto-remediation. Act as a technical reference and sparring partner across Ceph, storage, automation and AI tooling , document technical decisions and share your knowledge with the team. What we offer Exceptional team spirit across all departments and national borders; we live #OneTeam Exciting work in a highly innovative and international environment with cutting-edge technologies 32 vacation days, increasing with length of service Flexible working hours, home office options, and a secure permanent position with market- and performance-based compensation Employer-funded pension plan and an attractive insurance package OVHcloud covers 50% of public transportation costs Up to €400 annual financial contribution from OVHcloud towards sports activities (gym membership, sports classes, etc.) Through Corporate Benefits, you receive attractive discounts at numerous shops and companies We contribute to the leasing of your cargo bike Regular company events and free cold and hot beverages Several years of hands-on experience as an SRE, Storage Engineer or Platform Engineer running production storage infrastructure, with solid experience deploying, operating and debugging Ceph in production. You know the Ceph fundamentals from real-world operations: CRUSH, pools and placement groups, replication vs. erasure coding, BlueStore, scrubbing, recovery and backfill under load . You have managed storage infrastructure end to end , from the physical layer with drives, firmware, BIOS, controllers and hardware diagnostics through rebalancing, host drains, capacity expansion and hardware generation migrations. You are comfortable using Kubernetes as a control plane , not only as a workload runtime, and understand operators/controllers, custom resources, reconciliation and GitOps. You can also move confidently around OpenStack and debug issues involving Ironic, Neutron, Nova or Glance when needed. You have dealt with situations where durability really matters – such as degraded or near-full clusters, recovery under load or split-brain conditions – and you are used to making changes in a staged, evidence-based and reversible way. You have strong Linux and bare-metal skills , understand the block layer, filesystems and I/O behaviour, and are comfortable working with Ansible, Terraform and GitOps . AI-assisted engineering is already part of your day-to-day work. You have practical experience with LLMs and agentic tools and know where they can meaningfully support development, testing, reviews or operations. Ideally, you also bring experience with RGW / S3, RBD mirroring, CephFS or ceph-csi , deeper OpenStack storage integrations and Go and/or Python. Experience around VLAN/BGP, storage performance tuning, NVMe/BlueStore, observability, data protection, encryption, auto-remediation, security baselines or multi-site storage is also relevant for the role. You work autonomously, bring a strong sense of ownership , and are comfortable debugging problems where the actual root cause may sit somewhere between storage, networking, Kubernetes and OpenStack. You would rather verify what is happening from evidence than assume how the system should behave. We work in an international environment in English , so you should feel comfortable discussing technical topics, documenting decisions and working with the team in English. Unser Ziel ist es, eine effiziente und serviceorientierte Unterstützung sicherzustellen, Vertriebsaktivitäten zu fördern und unsere Prozesse kontinuierlich weiterzuentwickeln. Je nach Interesse und aktuellem Bedarf kannst du als Werkstudent (m/w/d) Einblicke in unterschiedliche Themenfelder gewinnen und dort aktiv mitarbeiten – von Social Media und digitalen Vertriebsmaßnahmen über die Organisation von Webinaren bis hin zur Datenpflege, Excel-Auswertungen, Partneranbindungen und vertriebsnahen Administrationsprozessen. Deine zukünftigen Aufgaben Du unterstützt unser Team bei der Bearbeitung von Anfragen unserer Vertriebspartner und internen Vertriebseinheiten zu Prozessen, Systemen und organisatorischen Themen. Eigenständig recherchierst du Informationen, bereitest Auswertungen und Präsentationen auf und unterstützt bei vertriebsrelevanten Projekten und Kampagnen. Gemeinsam mit verschiedenen Fachbereichen arbeitest du an der Koordination und Umsetzung vertrieblicher sowie organisatorischer Maßnahmen. Mit deinen Ideen wirkst du an der Analyse, Optimierung und Digitalisierung von Prozessen und Arbeitsabläufen mit. Darüber hinaus übernimmst du administrative Aufgaben, pflegst Dokumentationen und unterstützt im Tagesgeschäft. Das bringst du mit Du bist noch für mindestens zwei Semester immatrikuliert, idealerweise in einem wirtschaftsnahen Studiengang. Viel wichtiger als dein konkretes Studienfach sind jedoch dein Interesse an vertriebsnahen Themen, deine Lernbereitschaft und die Motivation, dich in neue Aufgabenfelder einzuarbeiten. Eine strukturierte, zuverlässige und eigenverantwortliche Arbeitsweise zeichnet dich aus. Auch bei mehreren parallelen Aufgaben behältst du den Überblick. Du kommunizierst freundlich, professionell und serviceorientiert mit verschiedenen Ansprechpartnern und hast Freude am Austausch mit Menschen. Verhandlungssichere Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift (mindestens C2-Niveau) sowie ein sicherer Umgang mit Microsoft Office, insbesondere Excel, Outlook und PowerPoint, gehören zu deinem Profil. Interesse an Digitalisierung, Automatisierung und KI-Technologien sowie die Motivation, Prozesse aktiv weiterzuentwickeln, runden dein Profil ab. Neugierig geworden? You distill SOTA research into robust, production-ready code optimized for sub-millisecond latency. At adjoe, that means architecting sophisticated auction mechanics, real-time bidding engines, and allocation algorithms serving millions of requests across a stack built on 770 million users. Deep expertise in Reinforcement Learning and Optimization. You have hands-on, deep theoretical and technical expertise in objective-based optimization, control theory, or RL applied specifically to bidding, pricing strategy, and budget pacing under extreme production constraints. Mastering high-dimensional data at scale. Large-scale Bayesian inference and handling sparse, high-dimensional advertising data are core to your work. You are strongly proficient in Python and related stacks, and know exactly how to architect scalable data pipelines to feed real-time optimization models. Raises the technical bar around them. Oversee accounts payable, accounts receivable, expense management, and vendor payments. Integrate external tools and applications with accounting systems such as QuickBooks Online to streamline workflows. Prepare accurate and organized financial records for annual reviews and external CPA firms. Support leadership with budgeting, financial forecasting, and cash flow planning. Advanced experience with QuickBooks Online or a comparable accounting platform, including integrating third-party applications. jobs.title: Senior Mechanical Design Engineer (Power Electronics)
jobs.description: Hyperscale Power is building the power backbone for the AI data center era: a complete power conversion chain from 13.8kV–35kV medium-voltage AC down to 800V DC, combining ultra-compact SiC-based power blocks. Our Solid-State Transformers (SSTs) are the core of this revolution, providing unprecedented control, efficiency, and compactness. As a Senior Mechanical Design Engineer, you will turn our power electronic modules into a robust, compact and safe product. You will design how the SiC-based power modules, magnetics, busbars and cooling come together into one unit, working closely with our power electronics, magnetics and thermal engineers. Instead of handing your designs over for someone else to build, you take them all the way: you calculate them, build and assemble the prototypes yourself in our workshop, and take the design from first prototype to a product ready for series production. This role is for you if… you've designed the mechanical integration of power electronics or other electronic systems and know your way around creepage, clearance and insulating plastics. You back your designs with solid calculations, and you're as comfortable with a screwdriver in the workshop as with CAD at your desk. This role isn't for you if… your experience is in classic mechanical design only, such as gears, gearboxes or pumps, or you prefer to stay at your desk while someone else builds your prototypes. It's also not a fit if you need technicians for assembly or established processes before you can start. Key Responsibilities Design the mechanical integration of power electronic modules into the SST: enclosures, holders, fixtures and jigs, and interfaces to the busbar system, with a modular design approach. Model and design electro-mechanical parts and assemblies, including plastics, sheet metal, insulation systems, magnetic components and cooling system interfaces. Ensure electrical safety through the design on both the medium-voltage and low-voltage side: creepage and clearance distances, CTI and material selection, electrical isolation and sealing. Design for manufacturing, assembly and test from the first concept, working with suppliers on processes such as injection molding, sheet metal and machining. Own the DFMEA for your designs and drive the resulting actions into the design. Validate designs with structural FEA, including static, modal, shock and vibration analysis, before they are released for production, and correlate the results with test data. Build and assemble prototypes and test assemblies hands-on in our workshop, together with the engineering team, using additive manufacturing where it speeds things up. Proven experience applying DFM and DFA to your own designs, with parts and assemblies that made it into production. Hands-on experience leading or actively contributing to DFMEAs. Strong experience with structural FEA (e.g. ANSYS), including static, modal, shock and vibration analysis. You set up the models yourself and use the results to drive design decisions. Solid knowledge of creepage, clearance, CTI, insulation coordination and electrical safety (e.g. IEC 60664-1, IEC 62477-1), ideally up to medium voltage. Solid experience designing with polymers/plastics, ideally for electronics integration. Proficiency in 3D CAD (e.g. SolidWorks), GD&T and tolerance stack-up analysis. Hands-on experience building and assembling prototypes in a professional setting. Experience with environmental, reliability and safety standards for power delivery products. Basic understanding of electrical design fundamentals; familiarity with PCBAs and PCBA components. Strong organization, written and verbal communication skills. Fluent English; German is a plus. Experience with high-volume manufacturing and automated assembly processes. Experience with additive manufacturing (e.g. SLA, SLS, FDM) for prototypes, fixtures and jigs, ideally including insulating or flame-retardant materials. Experience with PFMEA, DFT and DFR. Experience with insulation design for medium voltage, including partial discharge. Experience with liquid cooling integration or CFD. Benefits Equity + competitive salary. jobs.title: IT Operations Engineer
jobs.description:
At IMC, technology is not a department; it’s at the heart of everything we do. Developed in-house, our innovative software makes millions of trading decisions daily, and we win by making better and faster decisions than our competition. Our on-site IT Support team helps us move at a higher pace and quality each day, from hands-on support for end users to configuring and automating our systems to scale our support capabilities.

In this fully on-site position, you are the first person people come to with any IT issue, whether it’s a MacBook, a SaaS application, identity and access management, or hardware and AV. You support our growing Zug office and act as first- to third-line support. Our environment is predominantly macOS and cloud-based, with a small Windows footprint. You’ll work across a wide range of SaaS and custom systems. To succeed and grow, you take ownership, work autonomously, and keep improving an IT environment that runs smoothly and is ready to scale.

Your Responsibilities:

  • First-to-third line support for our users, mainly on macOS.
  • Managing and supporting our end-user platform, including Microsoft 365, Okta (SSO, MFA, lifecycle management), Slack and the Atlassian stack (Jira, Confluence, Jira Service Management).
  • Device management and patching: Jamf for macOS and Intune for phones, including enrollment, configuration profiles, app deployment and compliance.
  • Onboarding and offboarding, including account provisioning, access management and device setup.
  • Installing, setting up and servicing hardware and peripherals, including laptops, monitors, printers, and audio and video conferencing systems.
  • Troubleshooting, escalating and documenting network and connectivity issues.
  • Automating repetitive tasks and keeping knowledge base articles and runbooks in Confluence up to date.
  • Organizing and performing desk moves, room setups and physical equipment moves.
  • Everything else that keeps us moving.

Your Skills and Experience

  • A degree in an ICT-related field (BSc level ideally), or an equivalent qualification such as Informatiker/in EFZ.
  • At least one year of experience in a similar role in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong macOS knowledge and hands-on experience with JAMF (Pro).
  • Experience with Microsoft 365 administration and Intune; working knowledge of Windows.
  • Familiarity with Okta or a similar identity provider (SSO, SCIM, MFA).
  • Experience administering or supporting Slack and the Atlassian suite.
  • Scripting experience (Bash, Zsh, Python or PowerShell) is a plus, and so is Linux experience.
  • Excellent troubleshooting and diagnostic skills, with the ability to solve problems creatively and proactively.
  • Willingness to take on physical tasks such as desk moves and room setups.
  • A strong drive to grow (at IMC we are committed to helping with that).
  • You work autonomously, with a sense of urgency, and prioritize based on business needs.
  • Available and willing to work on-site full-time in Zug.
  • Proficient in written and spoken English; German is a plus.

About Us

IMC is a research-driven trading firm where quantitative modeling, machine learning, and engineering shape how modern markets are traded. A stabilizing force in markets since 1989, we provide liquidity across trading venues, delivering the best outcome in value and risk management to investors. Using our own technology and capital, we build proprietary systems and algorithms that operate across global markets. Our researchers, traders, and engineers work as a collective, combining rapid experimentation, advanced infrastructure, and real-time feedback to turn insight into execution and execution into advantage.

A proven track record in senior technical leadership positions such as Lead Engineer, Engineering Manager, Chief Engineer or Technical Superintendent. Expert knowledge of LNG regasification systems, cryogenic processes, boil-off gas management and associated marine and terminal systems. Extensive experience in asset integrity management, reliability engineering, maintenance strategies and HSE management frameworks. Strong knowledge of relevant European and German regulatory frameworks, technical and safety codes, classification requirements and permitting processes. Demonstrated ability to make autonomous, high-impact (technical) decisions under time pressure in safety-critical and mission-critical environments. Experience working with regulatory authorities, classification societies, engineering contractors, suppliers and gas grid operators. Strong commercial awareness and experience assessing investments, CAPEX and OPEX proposals and engineering/design modifications. Excellent leadership, communication and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to influence both senior management and operational teams. Fluent written and spoken English; German language skills would be a significant advantage. jobs.title: Verkaufsberater:in mit Stv. Funktion
jobs.description: Arbeitsbeginn Anfang März 2027 · 80–100 % Pensum · St. Gallen Bei alunir glauben wir an die kleinen magischen Momente im Alltag. Mit unseren bedeutungsvollen Schmuckstücken möchten wir nicht nur Freude schenken, sondern auch etwas Gutes bewirken. Für unseren alunir Store in St. Gallen suchen wir eine herzliche, engagierte und verantwortungsbewusste Persönlichkeit, die unser Team bereichert und gemeinsam mit uns besondere Einkaufserlebnisse schafft. Als Verkaufsberater:in mit Stv. Funktion unterstützt du die Store Managerin bei der Führung und Organisation unseres neuen Standorts, übernimmst Verantwortung im Tagesgeschäft und sorgst gemeinsam mit deinem Team für ein besonderes Einkaufserlebnis. Deine Mission ✨ Du unterstützt die Store Managerin bei der operativen und organisatorischen Führung des Stores. Bei ihrer Abwesenheit übernimmst du die Verantwortung für das Tagesgeschäft und bist die erste Ansprechperson für dein Team. Du bist aktiv im Verkauf tätig und begeisterst unsere Kundinnen und Kunden mit persönlicher Beratung und echter Gastfreundschaft. Du unterstützt bei der Führung, Motivation und Einarbeitung der Mitarbeitenden und lebst unsere Werte und Qualitätsstandards vor. Du erkennst Handlungsbedarf, setzt Prioritäten und sorgst für reibungslose Abläufe im Store. Du kümmerst dich um das Waren- und Lagermanagement sowie eine ansprechende Warenpräsentation. Du unterstützt bei organisatorischen Aufgaben wie der Personaleinsatzplanung und bringst eigene Ideen zur Weiterentwicklung des Stores ein. Was du mitbringst 💫 Mehrjährige Erfahrung im Detailhandel, idealerweise in der Schmuck-, Mode- oder Lifestylebranche. Erste Führungserfahrung oder die Motivation, den nächsten Schritt in eine Führungsposition zu machen. Freude daran, Verantwortung zu übernehmen, Menschen zu motivieren und im Team zusammenzuarbeiten. Eine herzliche, offene Persönlichkeit mit ausgeprägter Kundenorientierung. Selbstständigkeit, Organisationstalent und ein hohes Verantwortungsbewusstsein. Ein gutes Gespür für Ästhetik und Warenpräsentation. Fliessende (Schweizer-)Deutschkenntnisse und gute bis sehr gute Englischkenntnisse. Flexibilität und Bereitschaft für regelmässige Samstagseinsätze. Und natürlich eine grosse Portion alunir Magie. ✨ Deine ersten Monate 🌙 Dein Abenteuer bei alunir beginnt Anfang März 2027 in unserem Store in St. Gallen. Während deiner sorgfältigen Einarbeitung lernst du unsere Schmuckstücke, Abläufe, Werte und die alunir Philosophie kennen. Du wirst Schritt für Schritt in deine Aufgaben eingeführt und erhältst die Möglichkeit, unser eingespieltes Team und den Storealltag kennenzulernen. Gemeinsam mit der Store Managerin wächst du in deine Stellvertretungsfunktion hinein, übernimmst zunehmend Verantwortung und bringst deine eigenen Stärken und Ideen in den Storealltag ein. Was wir dir bieten 💛 Eine unbefristete Anstellung mit fünf Wochen Ferien und attraktiven Mitarbeitendenrabatten. Eine abwechslungsreiche Position mit Verantwortung und Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten. Die Möglichkeit, in einem bestehenden Store Verantwortung zu übernehmen und dessen Weiterentwicklung aktiv mitzugestalten. Ein herzliches, familiäres Team mit flachen Hierarchien und kurzen Entscheidungswegen. Eine sorgfältige Einarbeitung und persönliche Begleitung. Raum für eigene Ideen und persönliche Weiterentwicklung. Ein inspirierendes Arbeitsumfeld in einem Schweizer Schmucklabel, das mit jedem verkauften Schmuckstück auch etwas Gutes bewirkt. Bereit, mit uns ein neues Kapitel zu schreiben? ✨ Du liebst Schmuck, begeisterst gerne Menschen und möchtest in einem herzlichen Team Verantwortung übernehmen und etwas bewegen? Dann werde Teil von alunir und gestalte gemeinsam mit uns besondere Momente in unserem Store in St. Gallen. Schick uns deinen Lebenslauf und ein persönliches Anschreiben / Motivationsschreiben: Was sollten wir über dich wissen, und was macht diese Stelle bei alunir für dich passend? Wir möchten einen ehrlichen Eindruck von dir als Mensch bekommen – mit deinen Stärken, Eigenheiten und dem, was du noch lernen möchtest. Wir freuen uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen! 💛 Find more English Speaking Jobs in Switzerland on Arbeitnow

jobs.title: Senior Applied Scientist, Efficient LLM Inference & Model Optimization
jobs.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The role

Nebius Token Factory is looking for scientists who can turn frontier LLM and VLM inference bottlenecks into research questions, conduct rigorous experiments, and translate their findings into production capabilities. You will own focused research and optimization projects, write strong code, and produce prototypes, publications, and technical artifacts that engineers can build on.

Your research will span quantization, distillation, speculative decoding, KV-cache optimization, and model/runtime co-optimization, alongside inference engines and distributed inference architectures. You will investigate how these approaches interact, evaluate their trade-offs across model quality, latency, throughput, memory footprint, and cost per token, and work with engineering teams to bring promising results into production.

Your responsibilities

  • Lead research projects in efficient LLM and VLM inference, from hypotheses and experiments through ablations, prototypes, and production handoff.
  • Develop and evaluate methods spanning quantization, quantization-aware training (QAT), distillation, speculative decoding, KV-cache reuse, KV-cache compression, long-context inference, MoE routing, and model/runtime co-optimization.
  • Build prototypes using PyTorch, Triton, CUDA-adjacent tooling, or inference-serving frameworks, and collaborate with MLEs and platform engineers to turn them into production components.
  • Research LLM request routing and scheduling strategies, including cache-aware load balancing and prefill–decode disaggregation (PDD). Evaluate how queueing, KV-cache transfer, worker placement, and prefill/decode capacity allocation affect latency, throughput, and serving cost.
  • Investigate multi-node inference for dense and mixture-of-experts models, including wide expert parallelism (WideEP). Study expert placement, load imbalance, and computation/communication trade-offs, and use the findings to guide model and system architecture choices.
  • Develop rigorous evaluations covering quality, latency, throughput, numerical stability, memory footprint, tail latency, and cost per token. Compare serving architectures under consistent workload conditions and GPU budgets.
  • Work with MLE, GPU kernel, backend infrastructure, product, and customer teams to select research priorities with measurable production impact.
  • Share results through internal reports, technical blogs, papers, and open-source artifacts, and mentor engineers and scientists on experimental design, scientific rigor, and model/system trade-offs.

Must-haves

  • A PhD in computer science, machine learning, ML systems, computer systems, computer architecture, electrical engineering, applied mathematics, or a closely related discipline.
  • A strong publication record or equivalent research artifacts in ML, ML systems, efficient inference, model compression, quantization, distillation, serving systems, or related areas.
  • Strong Python and PyTorch implementation skills, with the ability to turn ideas into experiments and working prototypes.
  • Deep knowledge of LLMs, VLMs, transformer inference, decoding algorithms, model compression, quantization, and production-serving trade-offs.
  • Strong experimental design skills covering ablations, baselines, metrics, statistical reasoning, and failure analysis.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication.

Nice-to-haves

  • First-author publications at venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, MLSys, ACL, EMNLP, ASPLOS, OSDI, SOSP, ISCA, or HPCA.
  • Experience deploying ML models or inference optimizations in production.
  • Experience with vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, NVIDIA Dynamo, FlashAttention, FlashInfer, Triton, CUDA, or PyTorch internals.
  • Experience applying post-training, SFT, DPO, RLHF, RLAIF, preference optimization, or synthetic data generation to inference quality or efficiency.
  • Open-source research artifacts, widely used benchmarks, technical blogs, or invited talks demonstrating contributions to efficient AI systems.
  • Research or implementation experience in one or more areas of distributed inference system architecture, such as LLM request routing, PDD, multi-node serving, or MoE expert parallelism, including WideEP.

Benefits & Perks:

  • Competitive compensation
  • Career growth and learning opportunities
  • Flexibility and ownership
  • Collaborative and innovative culture
  • Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects
  • International environment and talented teams

What's it like to work at Nebius:

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

Develop and maintain embedded communication software across ground stations, radio equipment, and onboard systems. Diagnose complex failures across firmware, networking, operating systems, and hardware interfaces, working closely with our RF/electrical engineer. Improve communication reliability, latency, throughput, connection establishment, and recovery from interruptions. Build diagnostic tools, logging, and automated tests that make failures reproducible and improvements measurable. Own software integration and validation, from controlled lab experiments to real-world field testing. Maintain our modifications to supplier code, document architectural decisions, and work with suppliers to resolve platform limitations. Requirements Your Profile You combine strong software fundamentals with hands-on engineering judgment. You are comfortable working with incomplete documentation, questioning existing implementations, and designing experiments to establish why a system fails. Strong professional experience developing and debugging embedded software in C and/or C++. Demonstrated ability to understand and substantially modify complex existing codebases, such as vendor firmware, drivers, or communication stacks. Hands-on experience with embedded Linux and/or RTOS-based systems. Strong understanding of networking and communication protocols, including IP and serial interfaces. Experience investigating concurrency, timing, buffering, and resource constraints in embedded systems. A systematic approach to debugging, using tools such as debuggers, packet captures, and runtime traces. Proficiency in Python for diagnostics, tooling, and test automation. Ability to take ownership of an open-ended technical problem and carry it through implementation, testing, and field validation. MSc or PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Embedded Systems, or a related field, or equivalent demonstrated engineering experience. jobs.title: Software Engineer, Robot Autonomy (Planning & Navigation)
jobs.description: Our Mission At Laelaps AI, we believe robotics is entering a transformative decade, much like the arrival of the internet. Advances in AI, cloud computing, and hardware are reshaping what autonomous systems can do. Our mission is to build the intelligent software that powers physical security in the real world - enabling robots and sensors to handle dangerous and critical tasks that humans shouldn't have to. By engineering the orchestration layer for intelligent security, we aim to create a world that is safer, more secure, and more resilient. We're a strong founding team based in Zurich, backed by visionary investors and advisors. We are engineering the future of security today! The Role As a Software Engineer on Robot Autonomy, you will make our robots navigate dependably across real customer sites. Our stack works. The gap between working and dependable is the whole job. Every new site tests how a robot understands its surroundings and chooses where to go: a ramp the planner avoids, a narrow passage that exposes a poor route, a gate that changes the map, a person who steps into the robot's path, or localization drift that builds over a long patrol. You treat those cases as the real navigation problem to solve, not as edge cases. You'll shape the technical choices behind reliable navigation, from sensor selection, ground segmentation, and traversability estimation to predicting how people and vehicles move and planning safe, efficient routes around them. The system has to work day and night, in challenging weather, across different embodiments and changing site conditions. We measure success by whether the robot completes its patrol on a live site, not by how it performs in simulation. What You'll Work On Navigation and path-planning design: how robots represent traversable space, select routes, avoid obstacles, and reach goals across complex sites. Sensor integration driven by navigation requirements, including what ground segmentation and traversability estimation need in day, night, and challenging weather. Environment understanding: how the robot distinguishes ground from obstacles and estimates which terrain is safe and practical to traverse. Behavior prediction: anticipate how people, vehicles, and other dynamic obstacles will move, and plan routes that stay safe and efficient around them. Field reliability: reproduce failures from deployments, find the root cause, and fix it at the right layer, from sensor data and maps to costmaps, planners, and recovery behaviors. Planning under imperfect localization: plans that stay useful when the state estimate drifts and the robot must execute routes in tight or dynamic environments, working with the rest of Robot Autonomy on localization and control. Validation on real robots: logs, simulation, and repeatable field tests to verify that design choices and changes hold across routes, lighting, weather, and site layouts. New autonomy capabilities: work with the engineers building the operator application and backend so operator requests and new robot capabilities rest on a sound navigation design. The field feedback loop: work closely with forward-deployed engineers to turn site issues into bugs, design changes, and improvements to the navigation stack. Regular site visits to build a practical understanding of how robots and sensors behave in real operating conditions. Who We're Looking For We're looking for an engineer who has taken a robotics system from unreliable to dependable and takes ownership beyond individual tickets. You can explain why you made a navigation design choice and what it costs. When a robot takes a bad route, you can tell whether the planner, the map, the state estimate, or the robot's behavior is at fault, and you fix the right one. You are comfortable in the field and want to understand how robots behave in real customer environments. Your Background A Master's degree or PhD in mechanical engineering, computer science, robotics, electrical engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Proven track record building and deploying navigation on ground mobile robots in the real world (3+ years or equivalent depth). Hands-on experience with mobile robot navigation and path planning: route or local planning, static and dynamic obstacle avoidance, costmaps, or recovery behaviors. Understanding of how mapping and localization affect navigation, and the ability to diagnose when a planning issue is actually caused by the map, the state estimate, or robot behavior. Understanding of how lighting, weather, terrain, and sensor limitations affect perception and navigation, with experience developing or validating systems for demanding real-world conditions. Hands-on experience with robotics sensors and hardware, especially LiDAR, IMUs, and cameras. You can investigate issues across software, networking, and hardware boundaries. Experience testing and debugging navigation on physical robots using logs, visualization, simulation, and repeatable field tests. Strong ROS 2, C++, and Python skills. Clear communication of navigation and path-planning design choices and their trade-offs. Willingness to visit customer sites regularly. Nice to Have Experience with legged robots or with more than one robot embodiment. Experience with Nav2 or a comparable navigation framework. Motion prediction or planning among people and vehicles, such as trajectory forecasting or socially aware navigation. Terrain mapping and traversability methods: elevation mapping, learned traversability, or semantic segmentation for navigation. Experience with night-time or all-weather sensing, such as thermal cameras or LiDAR in rain and fog. Background in security, defence, or other safety-critical robotics deployments. What We Offer Ownership: you are able to ship products and deliver project end-to-end. Mission: autonomous security that keeps people and critical sites safe, including in defence. Career path: a ground-floor seat with real runway. Prove your value and you will not have barriers to grow. Team: work directly with PhD-level co-founders in AI, Robotics, and Physics, alongside a strong (and fun) founding team. Compensation: Competitive equity/salary package Culture: International founding team that is serious about building but does not take itself too seriously. jobs.title: Senior Consultant (Strategy & Data/AI Transformation)
jobs.description:
Who is Artefact?

Artefact is a next-generation strategy and data consulting firm dedicated to transforming organisations through data and AI. We combine the rigour of top-tier strategy consulting with deep expertise in data, digital and analytics to help clients achieve tangible business impact.

With 2,500+ consultants, data scientists and engineers, we work with global leaders such as Samsung, L’Oréal, Orange and Sanofi. Our Swiss offices are at the heart of Artefact’s growth, advising clients on their most pressing strategic challenges — from AI strategy and governance to digital transformation roadmaps and new business model design.

Main Responsibilities

As a Senior Consultant in our Zurich/Lausanne office, you will work at the intersection of strategy consulting and data and AI delivery. You will:

  • Strategy Development: Work with client leadership teams to address high-stakes questions. How can AI reshape our business model? How should we govern and organise for data? Which strategic programmes deliver the most impact?
  • Structured Problem-Solving: Break complex challenges down into decisions a client can act on, combining consulting rigour with a working knowledge of what current AI can and cannot actually do.
  • Solution Design: Turn a business question into a solution shape — what data it depends on, what kind of platform or product it should sit on, and what “good” looks like once it is built. You will do this alongside our data scientists and engineers.
  • Project Delivery: Support engagements end to end, from hypothesis framing and market and competitor analysis through to data maturity assessments, client workshops, governance design and implementation roadmaps.
  • Client Engagement: Work closely with C-level stakeholders and business unit leaders. You will build trusted relationships, communicate recommendations with clarity, and keep the work aligned to what the client is actually trying to decide.
  • Knowledge & Practice Building: Contribute to the growth of Artefact's Zurich office by shaping new offerings, creating intellectual capital - frameworks, thought pieces, benchmarks - and taking part in business development.

Candidate Profile

We are looking for someone who can hold a technical position and a commercial one at the same time. The strongest candidates meet most of the following.

  • Education: A degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, Business, Economics or a related field.
  • Work Experience: Around three to five years in consulting, or in a technical/date-focussed role with client-facing responsibility.
  • Business Acumen & AI Fluency: A genuine dual affinity for business and technology. You are comfortable with modern data and AI concepts - generative AI and LLMs, retrieval, predictive machine learning, cloud platforms - and with what they cost and where they fail, not only with what they are called.
  • Technical Depth: You have built AI or data products, not only advised on them. You can explain why you chose which model you put on which part of the work, and what that choice did to both output quality and cost. You will not be writing production code in this role, but you should have the basic understanding.
  • Analytical & Problem-Solving Skills: Strong quantitative and analytical skills, and the judgement to know which number actually decides the question. You are comfortable getting to a defensible estimate with your assumptions stated out loud.
  • Communication & Interpersonal Skills: Excellent written and verbal communication. You enjoy working in teams and in front of clients.
  • Languages: Fluency in German/French and English, written and spoken, is strongly preferred..
  • Work Eligibility: You must be eligible to work in Switzerland.

Why Join Us

  • Strategy and the Build: Artefact is neither a traditional strategy consultancy nor a pure technology player. You will move between the boardroom and the build, and be expected to be credible in both.
  • Engineers, not hand-offs: Our 2,500 people include the data scientists and engineers you will work beside on the same engagement - not a delivery organisation you hand a slide deck to.
  • Zurich Office Impact: As part of a growing Swiss team you will have visibility and impact from the first day. You will help shape Artefact's footprint in the region and work directly with senior leadership.
  • Learning & Growth: Regular training in both consulting method and AI and data capability, combined with international exposure.
  • Culture of Doers: Innovation, action, collaboration. We are entrepreneurial and fast-moving, committed to delivering impact while supporting each other's growth.

This position is based in Zürich or Lausanne.

jobs.title: Senior Security Engineer, Software
jobs.description:
The Security Team of Scopely Explore (formerly known as Niantic) seeks a Senior Security Engineer to improve the security posture of our software development lifecycle, applications, and build infrastructure.

Scopely Explore, known for global hits like Pokémon GO, Monster Hunter Now, and Pikmin Bloom is now part of Scopely, home to games like Monopoly GO!, Stumble Guys, and Star Trek Fleet Command. Together, we engage billions of players worldwide, and we need your expertise to keep them safe!

Do you want to help secure one of the most widely used gaming platforms on the planet? We seek creative and dedicated engineers with excellent technical judgment, strong interpersonal skills, and an eagerness to embrace new technologies.

What You’ll Do

  • Implement and maintain agentic or AI-enabled workflows to speed-up common security tasks.
  • Perform security reviews and audits of platform and application software throughout design and launch.
  • Provide guidance and expertise to product and operations teams across Scopely.
  • Design, build and maintain automation and tooling that amplify the Security Team’s impact and improve the developer experience.
  • Drive initiatives in security architecture, application scanning, fuzzing, and other proactive defenses.
  • Contribute to hardening efforts across in-house libraries, CI/CD systems, and cloud/container environments.
  • Be responsible for third-party library reviews and manage vulnerability remediation.
  • Educate engineers on secure coding practices and help standardize security across teams.
  • Engage in red-team exercises and coordinate with internal teams and external pentesting partners.

Qualifications

  • Bachelors in Computer Science or related field
  • 5+ years of experience in a global company with cloud-centric infrastructure (preferably GCP).
  • You have implemented services and applications with the help of AI tools like Claude, Codex, OpenCode or Gemini and are adept in the use of these tools and adjacent technologies (RAG, MCP, etc).
  • You are capable of creating automation, agentic workflows and tooling to reliably solve problems that scale to the whole enterprise.
  • You have in-depth experience in hardening distributed web services, cloud services and platform architectures.
  • You can demonstrate strong programming skills (preferably Go or Java) and a deep understanding of common vulnerability classes and exploitation patterns across modern stacks.
  • Excellent communication skills and experience collaborating across distributed teams.

Bonus Points...

  • Have participated in red-team operations or managed mitigation tracking.
  • Possess deep familiarity with build systems, artifact repositories, or large-scale infrastructure.
  • Have delivered privacy-focused solutions for user-facing services.
  • Have experience in code quality management or security champion programs.
  • Have worked in a customer-centric engineering culture and value pragmatic, scalable solutions.
  • Can demonstrate hands-on experience or research in the area of AI security and safety.

About Scopely

Scopely is a leading video game and global interactive entertainment company, home to many of the world’s most beloved and enduring experiences, including two of the most successful mobile games of all-time “MONOPOLY GO!” and “Pokémon GO,” along with “Stumble Guys,” “Star Trek™ Fleet Command,” “MARVEL Strike Force,” “WWE Champions,” the Scrabble® franchise, “Yahtzee® With Buddies,” and many others. Across mobile, web, PC, and console, Scopely creates, develops, publishes, and live-operates one of the most diversified and award-winning portfolios in the games industry — bringing hundreds of millions of players together through a shared love of play.

Our platform brings together foundation-model machine learning, a scalable data generation engine, and a partnership track record exceeding $5B in collaborations across the world’s leading biopharma and tech organizations. We’ve recently closed an oversubscribed seed round partnering us with an elite group of sophisticated and dedicated VCs including DCVC, Nvidia’s Nventures, AIX, Yosemite among others. Neo-1 is our all-atom foundation model that combines state-of-the-art structure prediction and molecular generation in a single system. Neo-1 enables rapid exploration of chemical and structural space for high value, previously intractable targets, and in particular unlocks small molecule proximity therapeutics like molecular glues with AI for the first time. In parallel, we are developing an advanced structural interactomics platform built on proprietary XLMS technology and a lab equipped with next-generation mass spectrometry instrumentation. This platform produces proteome-scale maps of protein interactions and helps identify small molecules that modulate proximity. Die Position ist national ausgerichtet und eng mit der weiteren Wachstumsstrategie verbunden. Gesucht wird keine klassische Außendienstrolle, sondern eine vertriebsstarke Persönlichkeit, die neue Industriekunden systematisch erschließt, interne Fachbereiche zusammenführt und Mandate mit wirtschaftlicher Substanz entwickelt. Sie gestalten aktiv die zukünftige Marktposition des Unternehmens. Benefits Was diese Position bietet Sichtbarkeit Ihre Arbeit hat direkten Einfluss auf die Entwicklung eines bedeutenden Geschäftsbereichs. Unternehmerischer Handlungsspielraum Sie erhalten Freiräume, um Märkte zu entwickeln und eigene Ideen umzusetzen. Komplexe Vertriebsaufgaben Sie verkaufen keine Standardprodukte, sondern Lösungen mit hoher Relevanz für industrielle Kunden. Perspektive Die Position eröffnet langfristige Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten innerhalb einer großen Unternehmensgruppe. Stabilität Sie arbeiten für ein wirtschaftlich starkes Unternehmen mit langfristiger Marktpräsenz und hoher Kundenbindung. Vergütung Ein attraktives Vergütungspaket trägt der Bedeutung dieser Schlüsselposition Rechnung. The Vectra AI Platform delivers integrated signal across public cloud, SaaS, identity, and data center networks in a single platform. Powered by patented Attack Signal Intelligence, it empowers security teams to rapidly prioritize, investigate and respond to the most advanced cyber-attacks. For more information, visit www.vectra.ai.

Technical Account Manager

Your Role:

The Technical Account Manager (TAM) is a critical role at Vectra and is responsible for developing and managing Vectra’s customers in an assigned region. You will own the relationships with your customers, connecting with key business executives, security and IT stakeholders to develop an understanding of their strategic business needs and goals.

Your Impact:

Leveraging this customer knowledge and your expertise in Vectra products and cybersecurity, you will provide an ongoing adoption and industry best practices strategy to ensure your customers understand and maximize value from their investment in Vectra.

This role demands interaction with enterprises at the senior level (CISO), as well as with technical staff within the IT and Security organization.

Responsibilities:

  • Drive high touch customer success focusing on large and highly complex enterprise organizations
  • Lead customers throughout the entire customer journey: onboarding, value realization, adoption and expansion
  • Own the customer relationship, providing ongoing support and proactive leadership to Vectra’s customers, to drive high levels of customer satisfaction, deep engagement, and mutual success.
  • Conduct customer touchpoints, executive business reviews and proactively monitor customer health
  • Drive deep integration of the Vectra Cognito platform into our customer’s business processes and technical ecosystem to create and increase stickiness.
  • Identify and grow expansion opportunities within the customer base and collaborate with the sales team to facilitate growth attainment.
  • Identify and assess renewal risks; develop and collaborate with internal teams in executing the remediation plans.
  • Direct crisis and incident response with urgency, working cross-functionally to ensure timely resolution while communicating effectively with customers.
  • Identify, develop and implement repeatable programs and processes across your portfolio of customers to maximize product adoption and usage and achievement of customer’s business objectives.
  • Track, measure and report on key metrics such as: customer satisfaction, customer health score, adoption rates, etc.
  • Able and willing to travel for on-site customer visits as required (25- 50%)

Requirements:

Successful candidates will have a solid technical foundation in network security and enterprise software, a proven track record of successfully interfacing with customers on both technical and non-technical levels, strong business acumen and sales experience, and above all a passion for ensuring a top quality customer experience.

  • A minimum of 5 years of experience in enterprise subscription-based vendors in a customer-facing role (such as Technical Account Manager - TAM, Professional Services, Sales Engineering, or Strategic Customer Service)
  • Extensive experience as a hands-on CSM or TAM supporting high touch enterprise customers (Fortune 500 or other large companies)
  • Strong experience of security product lines (firewalls, sandboxing, SIEM, forensics-type platforms)
  • Strong Knowledge of TCP/IP, DNS, VPN and SSL technology
  • Strong understanding of current security technologies and risks
  • Project management skills with a high attention to detail
  • Experience in supporting customers with strong empathy AND passion for revenue and growth
  • Proven record of establishing and building successful C-level relationships
  • Service management minded with strong commitment to customer service
  • Excellent presentation and communication skills, both verbal and written
  • Excellent organizational, analytical, negotiation, and influence skills
  • Relevant Bachelor’s degree; preference for computer science or related degrees
  • Demonstrated ability to use AI-enabled tools to improve productivity, quality, decision-making, and customer outcomes—for example, ChatGPT Enterprise, Microsoft Copilot and AI-enabled analytics tools.
  • Comfortable using AI for practical work such as drafting customer communications, summarizing cases, analyzing trends, preparing reports, researching technical issues, and automating routine workflows.
  • Able to critically validate AI-generated outputs, apply sound judgment, and protect confidential and customer information.
  • Identifies opportunities to responsibly embed AI and automation into team processes and supports adoption of approved tools.

Specific benefits offered varies by location, but commonly include health care insurance, income protection / life insurance, access to retirement savings plans, behavioral & emotional wellness services, generous time away from work, and a comprehensive employee recognition program.

jobs.title: Security Engineer
jobs.description: About Unblu Unblu helps the world's leading banks and insurance companies deliver conversational finance solutions. We provide highly secure engagement and collaboration software, enabling financial institutions to enrich the digital experience of their clients. By choosing a career with Unblu you choose to join an international, and innovation-savvy company. With our head office situated in Basel, Switzerland and additional offices in Bulgaria, Germany, the UK, Canada and the USA, you’ll be joining an international team dedicated to shaping the future of digital engagement. While Unblu is run as an independent company with global scope, we are fortunate to have Swiss Post as our anchor shareholder, providing long term support and vision to the company. The Role We're looking for a Security Engineer to work alongside our SRE and engineering teams, embedding security across the full software development lifecycle. You'll own a mix of defensive operations and developer-facing security tooling, from WAF rule management and CVE triage to building the pipelines that keep our deployments safe by default. This role sits at the intersection of application security, platform security and operations. You'll partner closely with engineering to ship secure software, and with SRE when things need to be hardened or investigated. We run entirely in the cloud, with a strong focus on Google Cloud Platform (GCP). You'll report to our VP SRE. An on-call rotation shared with SRE may be part of this role; we'll finalize expectations with the successful candidate. Responsibilities Embed security practices throughout the software development lifecycle, from design review to production monitoring, working hands-on with engineering teams Build, maintain and evolve the security tooling in our GitLab CI/CD pipelines: SAST, DAST, dependency scanning, secret detection and container scanning Review Software Bills of Materials (SBOMs) for our applications, track supply chain risk and drive remediation of issues in third-party components Own CVE triage end to end: assess relevance, prioritize based on exposure and exploitability, and coordinate remediation with product teams Manage and tune our Web Application Firewall (WAF) rules, balancing strong protection against false-positive noise Run internal security audits, document findings clearly and work with teams to close gaps Coordinate our annual external penetration test end to end; review pen test reports commissioned by our customers, translate findings into actionable work and respond back to the customer Lead the technical investigation, containment and recovery of security incidents together with SRE Provide technical evidence for ISO 27001 and SOC 2 audits, DORA resilience testing and customer security questionnaires, together with our Compliance Manager Help run or grow our external bug bounty program (optional scope): triage reports, coordinate with researchers and drive fixes through engineering Requirements Practical, hands-on security experience in a SOC, incident response or security engineering context, where you've done the work, not just written policy A degree, recognized certification (OSCP, CISSP, GIAC or equivalent) or structured training in information security Comfortable working across the entire software lifecycle, shifting between developer collaboration, operations and governance Hands-on experience building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines, ideally in GitLab CI Familiarity with vulnerability scanners, SBOM tools (Syft, Grype, Trivy, Dependency-Track or similar) and WAF platforms (Cloud Armor, Cloudflare or similar) Working knowledge of GCP security primitives (IAM, VPC Service Controls, Cloud Armor, Secret Manager, Binary Authorization, Security Command Center); comparable experience in another major cloud is fine if you're ready to go deep on GCP A clear communicator who can explain risk to engineers in terms they'll act on, and present confidently to customer security teams and auditors Fluent in English; German or French is a plus Benefits An interesting and rewarding role in the Sales team in the world's leading live collaboration software manufacturer Direct reporting line to the VP SRE Work in a diverse environment: 30+ nationalities across 8 locations Competitive salary, 5-week holiday, and great referral bonuses Flexible working hours and a hybrid working environment Our office in Basel is next to the main railway station #LI-Hybrid Make sure to have a look at our Glassdoor page too - it will give you more insights into what it is like to work for us. Unblu is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We use Workable as our recruitment platform, which utilizes AI to help categorize and organize applications. However, every application is carefully reviewed by our HR team. We respect and seek to empower each individual and support the diverse cultures, perspectives, skills, and experiences within our workforce. Please note that due to the nature of our business, all new joiners will have to complete a detailed background check, further information can be requested. jobs.description:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The Product

In a rapidly evolving world, trust in AI depends on AI agents being grounded in fresh, verified real-world data. Search is the foundation that makes this possible.

We are building an agent-native search platform designed specifically for AI systems rather than human users. Our product provides programmatic, low-latency, and observable search APIs that AI agents use to retrieve, filter, and reason over real-world information at scale.

The Role

We are looking for a Staff Software Engineer to work on the indexing and data processing layer of a novel search engine tailored for agentic AI consumption.

In this role, you will focus on building systems that ingest, process, and organise massive volumes of data into efficient, queryable structures. You will work primarily on offline and nearline pipelines, ensuring that data is fresh, complete, and efficiently accessible by downstream retrieval systems. You will operate in an environment where throughput, scalability, and correctness are critical; designing systems capable of handling tens of gigabytes per second across continuously evolving datasets.

In this position, your responsibility will be to:

  • Design, implement, and operate large-scale indexing systems and data pipelines that sit at the core of our search infrastructure
  • Develop and optimise indexing strategies balancing performance, freshness, and resource efficiency
  • Work on storage formats, compaction strategies, and update mechanisms to keep data accessible and current

  • Define and implement observability primitives, including structured logs, metrics, and data quality signals across offline and nearline pipelines
  • Monitor throughput, resource usage, and cost, and drive optimisations when business needs require it
  • Collaborate with runtime and ML teams to ensure indexing outputs meet retrieval and ranking requirements
  • Enable safe experimentation on indexing strategies and data processing logic through controlled rollouts and clearly defined quality signals

You may be a good fit if you:

  • 8+ years of experience building production backend or data infrastructure systems

  • Strong understanding of distributed systems, fault tolerance, consistency, and scalability
  • Experience running production systems and handling operational incidents
  • Systems-thinking mindset and ability to reason about end-to-end data flows

Strong candidates may also have experience with:

  • Distributed data processing frameworks such as Spark, Flink, MapReduce, or Beam
  • Content systems including, scraping, proxying, or anti-bot infrastructure
  • Ad tech, social networks, or other large-scale content platforms

jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, LLM Inference Optimization
jobs.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The role

As a Senior Machine Learning Engineer on the Applied AI team at Nebius Token Factory, you will own model and endpoint optimization from model artifacts through production deployment. Your work will span model internals, quantization and model compression, speculative decoding, KV-cache optimization, inference engines, serving architecture, and benchmarking to improve latency, throughput, memory efficiency, GPU utilization, and cost per token while preserving quality and reliability.

You will work with kernel and platform engineers to investigate serving problems, compare configurations, and resolve performance and quality regressions. You will evaluate model- and engine-level optimizations together with distributed inference designs, including request routing, scheduling, prefill/decode coordination, and multi-node GPU execution. Your improvements will be validated through reproducible benchmarks and safe production rollouts under real-world workloads.

Your responsibilities

  • Own optimization projects for specific model families, customer endpoints, or serving backends.
  • Compare inference engines and recommend serving configurations suited to individual workloads.
  • Diagnose model-quality and performance regressions during production rollouts.
  • Improve LLM and VLM endpoint latency, throughput, memory efficiency, GPU utilization, quality, and cost per token.
  • Deploy, configure, benchmark, and extend engines such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, Triton Inference Server, and NVIDIA Dynamo.
  • Develop production model-compression workflows covering quantization, quantization-aware training, distillation, low-bit serving, and accuracy recovery.
  • Implement or integrate speculative decoding, draft-model approaches, KV-cache optimization, prefix caching, chunked prefill, continuous batching, and disaggregated prefill/decode serving. For prefill–decode disaggregation (PDD), evaluate KV-cache transfer, worker placement, and capacity balancing to determine which workloads benefit from the architecture.
  • Design and improve LLM request routers and scheduling policies that balance worker utilization, queueing, request characteristics, and KV-cache locality while meeting latency and reliability targets.
  • Scale dense and mixture-of-experts inference across multiple GPU nodes. Select and tune tensor, pipeline, data, and expert parallelism—including wide expert parallelism (WideEP)—with attention to hardware topology, expert load balance, and communication overhead.
  • Build reproducible benchmark harnesses measuring TTFT, TPOT, tokens per second per GPU, p95/p99 latency, GPU memory, reliability, and cost per token. Validate architecture choices under representative traffic and consistent GPU budgets.
  • Collaborate with GPU kernel and platform engineers to trace bottlenecks across model code, kernels, runtime, scheduler, gateway, and cluster layers.
  • Produce design documents, performance reports, rollout plans, and customer-facing technical explanations.

Must-haves

  • Strong engineering skills in Python and PyTorch.
  • Hands-on experience deploying or optimizing LLM, VLM, or high-throughput transformer inference.
  • Practical knowledge of at least one modern inference stack, such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, Triton Inference Server, NVIDIA Dynamo, Ray Serve, KServe, or an equivalent internal system.
  • A strong understanding of transformer inference bottlenecks involving KV cache, attention, memory bandwidth, batching, parallelism, and long-context serving.
  • Ability to quantify trade-offs among latency, throughput, quality, utilization, and cost.
  • Experience designing or optimizing distributed inference system architecture, with hands-on work in one or more areas such as request routing, distributed scheduling, PDD, multi-node inference, or expert parallelism.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills across research, kernel, infrastructure, product, and customer teams.

Nice-to-haves

  • Experience with quantization-aware training, post-training quantization, FP8, INT8, INT4, NVFP4, MXFP4, AWQ, GPTQ, or SmoothQuant.
  • Experience with distillation, speculative decoding, EAGLE, Medusa, multi-token prediction, or related inference acceleration methods.
  • Experience supporting agentic workloads involving tool calling, structured outputs, streaming APIs, high concurrency, and multi-step orchestration.
  • Familiarity with CUDA or Triton; the role does not require kernel engineering to be the candidate’s primary specialization.
  • Contributions to open-source projects such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, FlashInfer, LMCache, PyTorch, Triton, Ray, or KServe.
  • Implementation experience with cache-aware request routing, PDD, or WideEP, including diagnosing communication bottlenecks and load imbalance.
  • Familiarity with GPU communication libraries and interconnects, such as NCCL, NVLink, InfiniBand, or RoCE.

The backend is that core. It is a modular monolith in C#, .NET 10 and PostgreSQL, serving one quinn app for employers, employees and our own support team, Maestro for batch processing, and our AI agents. Development has started, and the foundations the platform will run on for years are being laid now. This role is fully focused on quinn ONE. Our existing products are not part of it. What you will own Backend modules, end to end. Design, build, test and run modules and the APIs they expose, from requirements to production, without waiting to be handed a ticket. The data. The PostgreSQL model the platform rests on: schema design, migrations, transactions, indexing, and the calculations that must be right to the cent. The foundations. Audit trail, logging, versioning of our APIs and services, and the database upgrades that keep the platform current. Reliability and security in production. Tests, observability, performance, and data protection by design: an API returns what is needed, not everything that is available. Root causes, not symptoms. The architecture, pragmatically. Module boundaries, dependencies, the shared core and the country layers, evolved with clear trade-offs rather than fashionable patterns. The engineering bar. Code review, design discussions, and mentoring the developers around you, in Zurich and in our Armenia team. Where the frontend ends, the backend begins. Our Product Frontend Engineer owns everything on the screen: the app, Maestro’s interface, the component library. You own everything behind it: the domain model, the payroll logic, the APIs, the integrations with authorities, insurers and banks, and the data. You agree the API contract together, and Product decides what gets built. How we work We are AI-native, operationally rather than as a slogan. AI is how a small team ships like a large one, and how one engineer can hold the standard described here. We expect you to live in these tools and build your own leverage with them: scaffolding, test generation, migration checks, and whatever else takes manual work out of the way. And we expect the judgement that comes with it. AI writes code that looks right and is subtly wrong: a transaction boundary in the wrong place, a migration that works on test data and locks a table in production. In payroll, an amount is either right or wrong. You take the speed and keep the standard. Your first year In your first month, you set up, learn the system and the people, and merge your first changes. Within 100 days, you have delivered the platform’s audit trail, tested and documented, and fixed the first risks you spotted on arrival. By month nine, you are the person the team turns to for the quinn backend, and a developer you mentored is delivering features on their own.
